<br />

Use the **Elements** panel to inspect and edit DOM elements.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Key Point:** You can also use **AI assistance** to understand your website's styling and element layout. See [AI assistance for styling](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/ai-assistance/chat#styling).

## Overview

The **Elements** panel provides a robust interface to inspect and manipulate the DOM. You can use the DOM tree, which resembles an HTML document, to select specific DOM nodes and modify them with other tools.

The **Elements** panel also has the following tabs that contain relevant tools:

- **Styles**:

  - [View and debug](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/css) CSS rules applied to an element from all style sheets.
  - Find any [invalid, overridden, inactive, or other CSS](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/css/issues) that don't work as intended.
  - Edit elements by [adding a declaration](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/css#declarations), [applying a class](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/css#classes), and by interacting with the [**Box model**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/css#box-model).
  - Access container editing options with [Badges](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/elements/badges) found in the DOM tree.
- **Computed** : [Lists resolved properties](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/css/issues#css-in-computed) applied to an element as they are rendered by Chrome.

- **Layout** : Contains options to modify [grid](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/css/grid#options) and [flexbox](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/css/flexbox#layout) overlays.

- **Event listeners** : Lists all event listeners and their attributes. Lets you [find the source of event listeners](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/easily-jump-to-event-listeners) and [filter for passive or blocking listeners](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/devtools-digest-2016-09#passive_event_listeners).

- **DOM breakpoints** : Lists DOM change breakpoints [added from the Elements panel](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/javascript/breakpoints#dom) and lets you enable, disable, remove, or reveal them.

- **Properties** : Select a DOM node to inspect and sort the object's [own and inherited properties](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/dom/properties#own-and-inherited).

- **Accessibility** : Lists elements that have ARIA labels and their properties. Lets you toggle and inspect the page's [accessibility tree](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/accessibility/reference#tab).

## Open the Elements panel

By default, when you [open DevTools](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/open) the Elements panel opens. You can also [inspect a node](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/dom#inspect) anywhere on the page to automatically open the **Elements** panel.

To manually open the **Elements** panel:

1. [Open DevTools](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/open).
2. Open the **Command menu** by pressing:
   - macOS: <kbd>Command</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>P</kbd>
   - Windows, Linux, ChromeOS: <kbd>Control</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>P</kbd> ![Command Menu with](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/elements/image/command-menu-elements.png)
3. Start typing `Elements`, select **Show Elements** , and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. DevTools displays the **Elements** panel in the **Drawer** at the bottom of your DevTools window.
